description: MATH-F V1 development benchmark. Small (16-problem) hand-written set used to validate the generator -> verifier -> retry -> trajectory -> metrics pipeline end-to-end. NOT a claim of broad mathematical capability (see README.md section 'Scientific Positioning'). `tactic_priority` orderings are a good-faith prediction of real Lean 4 + Mathlib behavior (e.g. 'decide'/'rfl' getting stuck on opaque free variables where 'ring'/'omega'/'simp' succeed) based on how Nat/Int are defined, chosen so this benchmark exercises first-attempt success, multi-attempt success, AND permanent failure. It has NOT been confirmed against a real Lean toolchain in the environment that produced this repository (no network access) -- see README.md 'Known Limitations'. `accepted_tactics` is consumed ONLY by the offline MockLeanVerifier for that reason; the real LeanVerifier ignores it entirely and asks Lean itself.

problems.informal_statement: 7 times 8 is 56, over the natural numbers.
Addition of natural numbers is commutative.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_003 (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a

metadata.note: decide/rfl are expected to get stuck on the opaque free variables a, b (no literal to reduce); ring/omega should close it. Demonstrates the retry path.

problems.informal_statement: Addition of natural numbers is associative.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_004 (a b c : Nat) : a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c

problems.informal_statement: Multiplication of natural numbers is commutative.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_005 (a b : Nat) : a * b = b * a

problems.informal_statement: Zero is a right identity for addition of natural numbers.

metadata.note: a + 0 = a is the base case of Nat.add's own recursive definition, so this is expected to be defeq and close on the FIRST tactic (rfl), unlike mathf_003/004/005.

problems.informal_statement: Multiplication distributes over addition of natural numbers.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_007 (a b c : Nat) : a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c

problems.informal_statement: Double negation is the identity on the integers.
Any integer minus itself is zero.

problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_010 (a b : Int) : a + b = b + a

problems.informal_statement: 100 minus 1 is 99, over the natural numbers.
Twice a natural number equals that number plus itself.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_012 (n : Nat) : 2 * n = n + n

problems.informal_statement: A natural number is at most itself plus any other natural number.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_013 (a b : Nat) : a ≤ a + b

problems.informal_statement: Conjunction is commutative, as a propositional tautology.
problems.lean_statement: theorem mathf_014 (p q : Prop) : p ∧ q → q ∧ p

metadata.note: decide is expected to fail here: p and q are arbitrary Props with no assumed Decidable instance, so Lean cannot even elaborate 'decide' (failed to synthesize instance) -- a TYPE_ERROR-flavored failure distinct from the TACTIC_FAILURE cases above.

problems.informal_statement: Every natural number is strictly less than 2 raised to that number. Included deliberately as a problem the V1 fixed-tactic-portfolio generator is NOT expected to solve (it requires induction, which none of decide/rfl/norm_num/ring/omega/simp/tauto/trivial/aesop perform on an unbounded universally-quantified goal on their own). This problem exists to exercise and demonstrate the failure/retry/REJECTED path end-to-end, per MASTER PROMPT section 27.

metadata.note: Real Mathlib has 'Nat.lt_two_pow' which would close this in one line, but our V1 generator never attempts named-lemma application -- only the fixed tactic portfolio. Expected to fail with V1's generator; a good candidate for V2 (an ATP/lemma-retrieval generator).
